audit.why: 50.83% over 2656 games. Levels 1-3 are free against a Sylas with no E, it balances at 4-5, and his level 6 and two-item bruiser build take it back.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads Skill|Jayce|Jayce|Skill|Skill|Jayce|Jayce, but whys[0] says you out-range a dash-less Sylas at level 1, whys[4] calls level 6 'a real spike... his first kill threat', spikes[2] says first item goes 'even instead of in your favour', and late says 'This is where it slips'.
audit.why: The chart gives Jayce both item stages and calls level 6 even, directly against its own captions. Packet reference chart Jayce|Jayce|Jayce|Skill|Sylas|Skill|Sylas matches the text.
audit.corrected: Sides re-set to Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Sylas.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six fields (spikes[1], mid, wants.foe[1], whys[1], whys[3], whys[4], breakdown.cooldowns) call Abduct a 'chain-pull stun' or 'dash + stun'. Riot's text for E: 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits.' There is no stun, and the pull moves SYLAS, not you.
audit.why: This is the calibration-list error class — a CC that does not exist, invented on the ability the whole page tells you to fear. It changes the play completely: you are never locked by Abduct, so your feet and your Hextech Capacitor swap speed still work and you can walk out of the follow-up instead of standing there waiting to die.
audit.corrected: Abduct described as pulling Sylas onto you with no stun, in spikes[1], mid and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal call despite Kingslayer being the reason he wins extended trades.
audit.why: Kingslayer (W) heals against champions and falls from 12s to 6s cooldown by rank 5, so late it is up for almost every trade. Grievous Wounds is the item decision this matchup hangs on.

audit.whatIsWrong: No numbers on the cooldowns the page tells you to track.
audit.why: Abscond/Abduct is 13/12/11/10/9s, Kingslayer 12s down to 6s, Chain Lash 10s down to 6s, Hijack 80/55/30s. The 13s E at rank 1 is the commit window.

edits.before: Sylas R copies YOUR ult, but your R is just a stance swap with no payload, so the steal is nearly worthless to him. The real Lvl 6 threat is his E1 dash in, E2 chain-pull stun, then Q + W burst all-in -- his first genuine kill window.
edits.after: Sylas R copies YOUR ult, but your R is just a stance swap with no payload, so the steal is nearly worthless to him. The real Lvl 6 threat is Abscond in, Abduct chaining HIM onto you, then Q + W burst -- and note there is no stun anywhere in it.

edits.before: Once Sylas hits 6 and has his E up, the lane tightens. His all-in is E1 (Abscond) to dash in, E2 (Abduct) to chain-pull and stun, then Q + W burst on top of you. His R can copy your ult, but your R is only a stance swap with no real payload, so that steal does almost nothing -- the danger is the E2 stun, not his ult. Hold Thundering Blow (Hammer E): the knockback shoves him off you and interrupts the follow-up mid-combo. Keep poking with gate-Q from max range so he takes damage walking into E range, and don't facecheck -- a Sylas who lands the full E2 stun kills you.
edits.after: Once Sylas hits 6 and has his E up, the lane tightens. His all-in is Abscond (E1) to dash in, Abduct (E2) to chain himself onto you, then Q + W burst on top. Note what Abduct is NOT: it pulls Sylas to you and applies no stun, so you are never locked -- your feet and your swap move speed still work. His R copies your payload-less stance swap and does almost nothing. Hold Thundering Blow: the knockback shoves him off mid-combo and his 13s E is already spent. Keep gate-Q poking from max range so he bleeds walking into E range.

edits.before: Land E1-E2 (Abscond into Abduct) to pull and stun you for a free Q-W combo, or use the E1 dash to dodge your orb
edits.after: Chain Abscond into Abduct to land on top of you for a free Q-W, or spend the E1 dash purely to dodge your gate-Q orb

edits.before: His level 6 is a real spike: E1-E2 chain-pull stun into Q-W burst gives him his first kill threat, while his R copying your payload-less stance swap adds nothing for you to fear.
edits.after: His level 6 is a real spike: Abscond-Abduct chains him onto you for a Q-W burst — no stun in it, so keep walking — while his R copying your payload-less stance swap adds nothing for you to fear.

edits.before: He gets a second rank of W to heal your poke, but you still have both forms and he has no E stun yet -- the lane is balanced here.
edits.after: He gets a second rank of W to heal your poke, but you still have both forms and his E is not online yet -- the lane is balanced here.

edits.before: This is where it slips. By two items Sylas plays like a bruiser: his W heals more than your poke removes, he kites your Hammer combo with two E dashes, and one landed E2 chain-pull is enough to delete your squishy frame. His R copying your stance swap still does nothing for him, but he no longer needs it -- his own kit out-sustains you. Win this in the first ten minutes on plates and a health lead, because once he's stacked you cannot 1v1 him -- peel with Thundering Blow and let your team punish him after he commits E.
edits.after: This is where it slips. By two items Sylas plays like a bruiser: Kingslayer is down to a 6s cooldown and heals more than your poke removes, so Grievous Wounds is mandatory, and he kites your Hammer combo with two E dashes. His R copying your stance swap still does nothing for him, but he no longer needs it -- his own kit out-sustains you. Win this in the first ten minutes on plates and a health lead, because once he's stacked you cannot 1v1 him -- peel with Thundering Blow and let your team punish him after he commits E.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — His dash, then a recast pull with no stun, 13s at rank 1. Bait it, then commit. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: Abduct has no stun. Riot's E text is 'pulling himself to an enemy he hits' — the pull moves Sylas, not you, and applies no CC. Seven fields on this page called it a chain-pull stun. whys[1] also says 'lacks the E2 chain-pull to punish' which is fine as written since it claims no stun.
